title: Kernel Curator + Decode Slice Coordinator for Opportunistic Speculative Routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce latency for tail requests by enabling opportunistic speculative decoding across heterogeneous kernels and devices while keeping cost and correctness guarantees. This ticket implements a Kernel Curator (KC) that picks kernel families based on sequence distribution and attention patterns, plus a Decode Slice Coordinator (DSC) that splits prefill work into timed slices so a lightweight speculative decoder can start early on a smaller device.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic policy for choosing kernel variants (FP16/INT8 fused attention, blocked vs fused matmul kernels) per-request that minimizes expected token-latency under memory and KV-cache constraints.
- Allow decode to begin on a different device/model variant after the first N prefill tokens (a slice) with acceptance metrics that ensure quality regressions are bounded.
- Establish safe, observable fallback behavior that routes to the canonical host model if acceptance checks fail.

Scope and non-goals:
- Includes runtime APIs, schedulers, and telemetry hooks.
- Does NOT include ML-model fine-tuning to improve cross-variant agreement (handled in a follow-up).

Acceptance metrics (proposal):
- early_accept_rate: fraction of speculative slices where acceptance score >= threshold (target >= 85% on internal workloads).
- topk_agreement_p95: 95th percentile agreement of top-3 next-token sets between speculative decode and canonical decode (target >= 92%).
- token_latency_95_delta: reduction in 95th percentile token latency vs baseline (target >= 18%).
- fallback_rate: fraction of requests that triggered fallback (target <= 8%).

Kernel Curator design summary:
- Inputs: model fingerprint, sequence_length_distribution (recent window), attention_pattern_hint (sparse/dense), device_memory_budget, prioritized_slo (latency/cost).
- Output: chosen kernel profile id (e.g., attn-v2-int8-block-32) and execution hints (batching preference, KV caching policy).
- Heuristics: prefer lower-latency fused attention for short contexts; switch to block-sparse kernels for long sparse attention patterns; prefer INT8 when sequence_length * batch_size produces significant memory headroom but measured quantization quality on eval set is acceptable.
- Safeguard: if chosen kernel family has unknown telemetry, route to a dry-run mode for 2k requests before full rollout.

Decode Slice Coordinator (DSC) summary:
- Rationale: full prefill on large models is costly; by slicing prefill into incremental windows we can start a lightweight decoder (smaller shader or CPU fallback) after the first slice and commit output if acceptance passes.
- Slice sizing: adaptive based on prompt length and estimated prefix entropy; default slice = max(8 tokens, 10% of prompt, capped at 64).
- Coordination: run prefill slice 0 on canonical host to compute stable KV snapshot; transfer compact KV fingerprints and small attention summaries to speculative host using RDMA/copy; speculative host runs decode for slice 1..M; acceptance checks compare soft-logprob delta and topk overlap between speculative and canonical partial decode.

Acceptance function prototype (high level):
- score = w1 * normalized_logprob_delta + w2 * topk_overlap + w3 * structural_match_score
- if score >= threshold then commit speculative result and merge KV caches; otherwise fallback to canonical decode and mark request for more conservative routing.

Fallback behavior and safety:
- Immediate fallback to canonical host if DSC detects mismatched sequence lengths or KV checksum mismatch.
- Circuit-breaker: if fallback_rate > 12% in a rolling 10k window, throttle speculative routing and alert SRE.
- Hard rollback: on customer-visible regressions (error budget or correctness SLAs), disable KC heuristics and revert to baseline kernel selector via runtime flag.

Telemetry and observability:
- Events: speculative_attempt, speculative_accept, speculative_reject, kernel_selected, kernel_dryrun_result, kv_transfer_time, slice_latency_ms.
- Dashboards: per-model speculative_accept_rate, fallback_rate, kernel_choice_distribution, cost_delta_per_1k_tokens.
- Traces: trace speculative path end-to-end with tags for kernel_id, slice_index, device_id.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit and integration tests: deterministic KV fingerprint tests; synthetic attention patterns with oracle canonical outputs.
- Perf bench: workload suite (chat-short, chat-long, code-completion) to measure token-latency P50/P95 and cost.
- Staged rollout: internal canary -> beta customers (opt-in) -> gradual ramp with automated gating on acceptance metrics.
- Duration: 3-week iterative rollout with metric gates every 24h.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Memory duplication vs copy-on-write for KV transfers: duplication is simpler but costs memory on speculative host; COW requires shared memory or RDMA.
- Acceptance thresholds tuning: aggressive thresholds reduce fallback but risk silent quality drops. We'll run offline calibration harness to pick w1,w2,w3.
- Kernel selector complexity vs maintainability: prefer rule-based + telemetry feedback loop over ML blackbox for initial launch.

Implementation notes (engineering checklist):
- [ ] KC: new runtime module under runtime/kernel_curator with selection API and dry-run toggles.
- [ ] DSC: scheduler under runtime/decode_slices that orchestrates cross-device slice handoff and KV fingerprinting.
- [ ] Telemetry: add events to tracing library and update ingestion schemas (metrics team coordination).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kC_kernel-curator-design (internal)
- Spec harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/spec-harness/pull/482 (WIP)
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1548
- Post-mortem template for fallbacks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Fallback+Runbook

Estimate and resources:
- Core implementation: 2 engs for 3 sprints (KC + DSC + tests)
- Telemetry + dashboards: 1 eng + 1 observability engineer
- QA and calibration: 1 eng + 1 research engineer for offline calibration runs

Definition of Done:
- KC and DSC implemented and covered by unit tests
- Telemetry emitted and dashboards available
- Acceptance metrics meet targets on internal workload suite
- Rollout plan executed with gating and a documented rollback procedure
acceptance_criteria: Kernel Curator returns kernel profile id within 2ms per request and passes dry-run evaluation on 2k sample requests
Speculative path acceptance rate >= 85% and topk_agreement_p95 >= 92% on internal suite
Fallback rate <= 8% and circuit-breaker configured at 12%
End-to-end P95 token latency improvement >= 18% vs baseline in experiment cluster
Dashboards and traces displaying speculative_* events and kernel distributions
implementation_notes: KC will expose select_kernel(model_id, context_hint) -> kernel_id, exec_hints
DSC will implement slice coordinator with backpressure-aware queue and a compact KV fingerprint format (sha256 truncated) for fast comparisons
Use existing kernel registry to map kernel_id -> capability matrix (supports_int8, supports_sparse_attn, mem_estimator)
Add dry-run mode where KC tags requests and records predicted latency/cost without switching production kernel
telemetry_goals: Emit speculative_attempt/speculative_accept/speculative_reject per request with kernel_id and slice_index
Track kv_transfer_time_ms and slice_latency_ms per device
rollback_plan: Feature flag to disable KC and DSC at runtime (immediate revert)
Automated job to reset kernel_selector to conservative-mode across nodes
Post-mortem & remediation checklist for correctness regressions
